Twisting and charge transfer in the difluoroboron dyes

Author

Giovanni Gravili

Published

November 13, 2026

Modified

November 23, 2026

Abstract

Whether the dimethylamino difluoroboron chelate, unlike the methoxy one, relaxes in acetonitrile into a twisted intramolecular charge-transfer (TICT) state: the calculations both chelates’ workflows run and what they will be compared on.

Keywords

TICT, difluoroboron chelate, charge transfer, natural transition orbitals

Status Workflow Description
Methoxy chelate in acetonitrile Sets the baseline with the S_0 and S_1 minima of \mathbf{1}, its twists about \mathrm{A} and \mathrm{B}_1 in both states, and the S_0 map of both twists.
Dimethylamino chelate in acetonitrile Tests whether the donor of \mathbf{3} turns perpendicular in S_1, and how much charge moves as it turns.

We study two of the difluoroboron chelates of Saito et al. [1] to test for twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) in acetonitrile, the solvent used here (Fig. 2):

  • The methoxy chelate \mathbf{1} emits strongly in acetonitrile, while the dimethylamino chelate \mathbf{3}, with the stronger donor, barely does; comparing the two separates the donor’s effect from what any such dye does.
  • In their calculation, the S_1 minimum of \mathbf{3} has its donor phenyl nearly perpendicular to the chelate ring, while that of \mathbf{1} stays close to its S_0 structure.

In the ground state, the donor lone pair pushes electron density across bonds \mathrm{A} and \mathrm{B}_1 into the electron-withdrawing \mathrm{BF_2}-\beta-diketonate core, keeping the conjugated rings planar (Fig. 3).

Upon photoexcitation to the coplanar locally excited (\mathrm{LE}) state, a strong donor–acceptor pair can twist about the connecting single bond into a perpendicular twisted intramolecular charge-transfer (\mathrm{TICT}) state, which returns to the ground state (\mathrm{GS}) through weak red-shifted fluorescence or non-radiative relaxation (Fig. 4).

The calculations follow Naito et al. [3], with TD-DFT [4], B3LYP [5], [6], [7] and the dielectric-dependent functional of Shimazaki and Tachikawa [8] in IEFPCM acetonitrile [9] with 6\text{-}31{+}\mathrm{G}(d); since these chelates can twist, the twists are also scanned.

How charge transfer is measured

The absorption and emission runs give, at the minima \mathbf{R}_0 and \mathbf{R}_1, the quantities other studies use to recognize charge transfer (Tab. 1); the scans follow some of them along each twist.

Absorption and emission at the minima

  • S_0 is optimized to \mathbf{R}_0 and verified; there the screening \varepsilon_s and the absorption \Delta E_{S_0\rightarrow S_1} are computed.
  • S_1 is relaxed to \mathbf{R}_1 and verified; there the emission \Delta E_{S_1\rightarrow S_0} is computed.
  • DD-DFT repeats the path with \alpha=1/\varepsilon_s from a self-consistent screening (Fig. 5).

Values from the literature

Saito et al. [1] report at the S_1 minima, with B3LYP/6\text{-}31{+}\mathrm{G}(d) in PCM acetonitrile:

If our runs agree with them, we expect:

  • \theta_{\mathrm{B}_1}(\mathbf{R}_1)\approx90^\circ for \mathbf{3}, and \theta_{\mathrm{B}_1}(\mathbf{R}_1)\approx\theta_{\mathrm{B}_1}(\mathbf{R}_0) for \mathbf{1}.
  • f_1(\mathbf{R}_1)\approx0 and a much larger \lvert\Delta\boldsymbol{\mu}\rvert for \mathbf{3}.
  • B3LYP possibly favouring the twisted \mathbf{3} too much, which the DD-DFT branch checks.

What the minima give

The B3LYP minima reproduce Saito et al. [1] (Tab. 3):

  • In \mathbf{1}, S_1 relaxes without twisting: the rings stay coplanar, \theta_{\mathrm{B}_1}(\mathbf{R}_1)=174.9^\circ, and the emission stays bright, f_1(\mathbf{R}_1)=1.20.
  • In \mathbf{3}, S_1 relaxes by turning the donor ring perpendicular, \theta_{\mathrm{B}_1}(\mathbf{R}_1)=-90.3^\circ, which switches the emission off, f_1(\mathbf{R}_1)=1.0\times10^{-4}, and separates the charge, \lvert\boldsymbol{\mu}_1(\mathbf{R}_1)\rvert=33.67\,\mathrm{D}.

Natural transition orbitals of \mathbf{3} at \mathbf{R}_0 and \mathbf{R}_1

The dominant hole \phi_\mathrm{h} and particle \phi_\mathrm{p} NTOs of \mathbf{3} change with the twist (Fig. 6):

  • At the planar \mathbf{R}_0, they overlap across \mathrm{B}_1.
  • At the perpendicular \mathbf{R}_1, they separate completely.

Twisting about the bonds \mathrm{A} and \mathrm{B}_1

  • From the B3LYP minima, the twist about \mathrm{A} or \mathrm{B}_1 is scanned over half a turn in 10^\circ steps, in S_0 and in S_1, with \Delta E_{S_0\rightarrow S_1} at each S_0 point (Fig. 8).
  • An S_0 map relaxes both twists together on a 30^\circ grid.

Each twist turns one group against the next across its bond:

  • \theta_\mathrm{A} turns the \mathrm{CH_3O} group of \mathbf{1}, or the \mathrm{(CH_3)_2N} group of \mathbf{3}, against the \mathrm{C_6H_4} ring it is bonded to.
  • \theta_{\mathrm{B}_1} turns that \mathrm{C_6H_4} ring against the \mathrm{BF_2O_2C_3H} chelate ring.

The angle decides how far the two \pi systems overlap:

  • At \theta=0^\circ or \theta=180^\circ, the two groups lie in one plane and their \pi systems overlap.
  • At \theta=90^\circ, they stand at right angles, and the excited electron can move wholly from the donor to the acceptor.
  • Fig. 7 shows both angles as each group turns; Naito et al. [3] and Sung et al. [12] compare the same angles between S_0 and S_1.

The chelate chosen in the menu turned rigidly about the chosen bond, in 10^\circ steps over half a turn from its S_0 minimum (or its starting geometry until that is optimized), with \theta_\mathrm{A}, \theta_{\mathrm{B}_1} and the lengths of both bonds measured at every frame; nothing relaxes, so it shows what the scans vary, not their result.

The scans then follow the energy along each twist (Fig. 8): the relaxed S_0 and S_1 profiles, the vertical excitation at each S_0 point, and the barriers read from them.

If \mathbf{3} twists into a charge-transfer state, we expect:

  • For \mathbf{3}, E_1(\theta_{\mathrm{B}_1}) falling towards \theta_{\mathrm{B}_1}=90^\circ with no barrier, \Delta E_1^{\ddagger}=0; for \mathbf{1}, rising or flat.
  • f_1 falling and \delta q_\mathrm{D} rising along the twist, more steeply for \mathbf{3}.

Energy along the relaxed S_1 scans

The relaxed S_1 and vertical S_0 energy changes follow each relaxed S_1 scan (Tab. 4, Fig. 9):

  • For \mathbf{1}, S_1 stays nearly flat about \mathrm{B}_1 while S_0 climbs: the twisted geometry is reachable in S_1 but nothing drives it there.
  • For \mathbf{3}, S_1 rises all the way from its perpendicular minimum, \Delta E_1^{\ddagger}=0: the twisted state is where S_1 relaxes, as a TICT state should.
  • About \mathrm{A}, S_1 rises for both chelates, so turning the donor group is not a relaxation path; the profile of \mathbf{3} jumps between two branches.

Brightness along the relaxed S_1 scans

The oscillator strength and the transition dipole follow each relaxed S_1 scan (Tab. 5, Fig. 10, Fig. 11):

  • Turning the rings perpendicular about \mathrm{B}_1 darkens S_1 in both chelates, but only \mathbf{3} relaxes there.
  • Twisting about \mathrm{A} leaves \mathbf{1} bright and \mathbf{3} dark.
  • \lvert\boldsymbol{\mu}_{01}\rvert falls with f_1, so the darkening comes from the coupling of the two states, not from the gap.

Donor charge along the S_0 scans

The donor charge in the S_1 density follows each S_0 scan (Tab. 6, Fig. 12):

  • Turning about \mathrm{B}_1 takes electron density off the donor in S_1 for both chelates, most at right angles.
  • Twisting about \mathrm{A} barely moves it.
  • Hirshfeld [13] and CM5 [14] give the same changes, so the trend does not depend on the partition.

Dipoles and donor charge along the relaxed S_1 scans

The S_0 and equilibrium-solvated S_1 permanent dipoles and the excitation donor charge change follow each relaxed S_1 scan (Tab. 7, Tab. 8, Fig. 13, Fig. 14):

  • About \mathrm{B}_1, both chelates reach large excited-state dipoles (\lvert\boldsymbol{\mu}_1\rvert\approx 45\text{–}48\,\mathrm{D}) and \Delta q_\mathrm{D}\approx 0.77\text{–}0.79\,e near 90^\circ, showing that the twisted state is strongly charge-separated even in \mathbf{1}, though only \mathbf{3} relaxes there.
  • About \mathrm{A}, \mathbf{3} stays charge-separated (\lvert\boldsymbol{\mu}_1\rvert=44\text{–}49\,\mathrm{D}, \Delta q_\mathrm{D}=0.57\text{–}0.82\,e) because its donor ring remains perpendicular, whereas \mathbf{1} keeps its rings coplanar and drops to \lvert\boldsymbol{\mu}_1\rvert=21.1\,\mathrm{D} (\Delta q_\mathrm{D}=+0.15\,e) at 90.2^\circ.
  • Hirshfeld [13] and CM5 [14] give identical \Delta q_\mathrm{D} at every geometry because the geometry-dependent CM5 correction cancels between S_1 and S_0.

B3LYP and DD-DFT with IEFPCM acetonitrile

Conventional hybrid DFT and its screening-weighted counterpart in a polarizable continuum.

Status Workflow Description
Methoxy chelate in acetonitrile Sets the baseline with the S_0 and S_1 minima of \mathbf{1}, its twists about \mathrm{A} and \mathrm{B}_1 in both states, and the S_0 map of both twists.
Dimethylamino chelate in acetonitrile Tests whether the donor of \mathbf{3} turns perpendicular in S_1, and how much charge moves as it turns.
NoteOngoing
  • With B3LYP, S_1 of \mathbf{1} is the bright HOMO-to-LUMO state, 2.96\,\mathrm{eV} in absorption and 2.65\,\mathrm{eV} in emission, and has a verified planar minimum.
  • In S_0, turning the methoxy group costs at most 20.5 and the donor ring about \mathrm{B}_1 32.9\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}, and the map’s single maximum of 47.0\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} is close to their sum.
  • Vertically, twisting about \mathrm{B}_1 darkens S_1, to f=0.008 at 100^\circ from 1.28 when planar, while turning the methoxy group raises it by 0.18\,\mathrm{eV} and keeps it bright.
  • Relaxed along \theta_{\mathrm{B}_1}, S_1 stays within 4.2\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} of its planar minimum and reaches a dark perpendicular point 1.9\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} lower, within the Fast level’s precision; relaxed along \theta_\mathrm{A}, S_1 rises by 37.4\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} at the perpendicular methoxy group and stays bright.
  • DD-DFT places S_1 0.37\,\mathrm{eV} higher with less charge transfer; its S_1 minimum awaits verification.

NoteOngoing
  • The S_0 minimum of \mathbf{3} is verified, its B3LYP screening is \varepsilon_s=2.90, and its bright S_1 absorbs at 2.53\,\mathrm{eV}, 0.43\,\mathrm{eV} below the methoxy chelate’s, with more charge transfer.
  • In S_0, turning the dimethylamino group costs 36.8\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}, nearly twice the methoxy group’s, as its nitrogen pyramidalizes, and vertically the turn hands the absorption from S_1 to S_2, f_1 falling to 0.03 at 120^\circ from 1.27.
  • Twisting the donor ring about \mathrm{B}_1 costs 45.7\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} in S_0, 1.4 times the methoxy chelate’s, yet vertically it lowers S_1 from 2.52 to 1.93\,\mathrm{eV} and darkens it to f=0.015 at the perpendicular geometry, where the vertical S_1 lies 11.9\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} below the planar one.
  • Over the S_0 map the twists are not additive: turning both perpendicular costs 65.2\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}, 17.5 less than the two apart, and vertically S_1 is dark wherever the ring about \mathrm{B}_1 is perpendicular or the dimethylamino group is 120^\circ into a sweep, on its uninverted branch.
  • S_1 relaxes into a twisted minimum, the donor ring perpendicular to the core about \mathrm{B}_1, where it is dark (f=1.0\times10^{-4}), only 1.38\,\mathrm{eV} above S_0 and carries a 33.7\,\mathrm{D} dipole; the DD-DFT branch was cancelled and waits to be submitted again.
  • Relaxed in S_1 along the twist about \mathrm{B}_1, S_1 falls without a barrier by 23.0\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} from the coplanar ring into the twisted minimum and darkens from f_1=1.03 to below 0.001, where the methoxy chelate’s stays flat within 4.2\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}.
  • Relaxed in S_1, turning the dimethylamino group keeps S_1 dark and costs up to 35.4\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} with the donor ring held perpendicular, while its perpendicular form on a coplanar ring, a second dark twisted S_1, lies 16.4\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} above the minimum, so the twist about \mathrm{B}_1 gives the lowest S_1.
